summary: This diff adds three new, additive automation scripts (audit_pipeline_master_orchestrator.py, generate_auditor_engine_master_report.py, close_phase8_master_orchestration.py) plus a plan-file status/evidence update and a generated JSON report snapshot -- no files under migrations/, schema, auth/, or any security/permission/payment/billing/rls path are touched, and .github/workflows/** is untouched, so tier1 is correctly assigned. The orchestrator shells out to existing sub-pipeline scripts via subprocess.run with argument lists (no shell=True, no string-built commands), uses parameterized SQL for all inserts, validates --domains input against a fixed key list, and serializes DB writes with an flock-based lock that is not held while spawning the report-generator subprocess (no self-deadlock risk). The report generator's JSON output is internally arithmetically consistent -- I independently re-summed by_severity, by_repo, and by_domain totals against the per-domain-repo breakdown and every total reconciles exactly, which is strong evidence this reflects a real aggregation run rather than fabricated numbers. Both new scripts have idempotent write logic (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, anchor-based YAML edit guarded by a 'already closed out' check) so re-running them is safe.
issues: generate_auditor_engine_master_report.py's _count_by() builds SQL via an f-string interpolating the column name directly into the query text; every current call site passes a hardcoded literal so there is no live injection vector, but it's a fragile pattern -- a future caller passing an unvalidated column argument would reintroduce a SQL-injection-shaped bug. Worth switching to a whitelist-checked column lookup before this helper is reused elsewhere.

No automated tests (unit or integration) were added for any of the three new scripts; correctness here is currently only demonstrated by the two live runs cited in the plan-file evidence block, not by a repeatable test suite.
